proofs.proof_tex:
By consistency and conditional exchangeability,
\[
 E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}=E_P(Y\mid A=a,X)=m_a(X),
\]
and overlap makes the latter conditional regression identified for every action. Hence the given functional \(W(\theta)=E_P\sum_a\pi_\theta(a\mid X)m_a(X)\) equals the causal welfare of rule \(\pi_\theta\); the following argument estimates this identified functional and does not define the causal equality into existence.

Write \(k_\theta(O)=\sum_a\pi_\theta(a\mid X)\log\{\pi_\theta(a\mid X)/b_a(X)\}\). The first-order condition from \(\textnormal{lem:penalized-cancellation}\) and differentiation under the bounded finite sum give
\[
 E_P D_c(O)=\nabla W(\theta_c)-c\nabla K(\theta_c)=a_c-cg_c=0.
 \tag{24}
\]
The foldwise conditional decomposition proved in \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\), at derivative order one, gives uniformly in \(c\)
\[
 \sqrt n\nabla\widehat M_c(\theta_c)
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nD_c(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{25}
\]
Here its conditional centered term is \(O_{\mathbb P}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n})\) by the envelope and entropy bounds, and its conditional mean is at most \(C_{\mathrm{sm}}\sqrt n r_{m,n}r_{e,n}=o(1)\) by \(\textnormal{ass:product-rate}\). The empirical divergence derivative is already the oracle empirical average and is included in \(D_c\).

Uniform localization and interiority, also proved in \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\), make the empirical first-order condition valid simultaneously in \(c\) with probability tending to one. Taylor's formula along the segment between \(\theta_c\) and \(\widehat\theta_c\) gives
\[
 0=\nabla\widehat M_c(\widehat\theta_c)
 =\nabla\widehat M_c(\theta_c)-\overline H_{n,c}(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c),
 \quad
 \overline H_{n,c}=-\int_0^1\nabla^2\widehat M_c(\theta_c+t(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c))\,dt.
 \tag{26}
\]
Uniform second-derivative convergence and localization imply \(\sup_c\|\overline H_{n,c}-H_c\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Since \(\lambda_{\min}(H_c)\geq h\), inversion in (26), (25), and tightness of the bounded Lipschitz class \(\{D_c:c\in\mathcal C\}\) yield
\[
 \sup_c\left\|\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)
 -n^{-1/2}\sum_iH_c^{-1}D_c(O_i)\right\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{27}
\]
This is the optimizer expansion because \(\psi_c^\theta=H_c^{-1}D_c\).

At derivative order zero, the same foldwise argument and the product-rate condition give
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat W(\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi_c^W(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)
 \tag{28}
\]
uniformly in \(c\). Since divergence has no learned nuisance,
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat K(\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)\}
 =n^{-1/2}\sum_i\phi_c^K(O_i)
 \tag{29}
\]
exactly. Taylor expansion, uniform gradient consistency, and (27) now give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\theta_c)\}
 &=n^{-1/2}\sum_i\{\phi_c^W(O_i)+a_c^\top\psi_c^\theta(O_i)\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
 \sqrt n\{\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)\}
 &=n^{-1/2}\sum_i\{\phi_c^K(O_i)+g_c^\top\psi_c^\theta(O_i)\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
where every remainder is uniform over \(\mathcal C\). These are precisely the \(\psi_c^W\) and \(\psi_c^K\) coordinates declared in \(\textnormal{def:joint-influence}\).

For the implemented-rule evaluations, subtract the population function at the same estimated argument. The mean-value identity gives
\[
 \sqrt n\left([\widehat W-W](\widehat\theta_c)-[\widehat W-W](\theta_c)\right)
 =\sqrt n\{\nabla\widehat W(\bar\theta_c)-\nabla W(\bar\theta_c)\}^\top
 (\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \tag{31}
\]
uniformly, because the gradient difference is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and (27) makes \(\sqrt n\sup_c\|\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Combining (31) with (28) proves the implemented welfare statement; the identical argument using (29) proves the implemented divergence statement.

We verify the process limit without importing an undeclared empirical-process theorem. The continuity of the optimizer path was proved in \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\). Uniform interiority makes its score vanish, and differentiating \(\nabla M_c(\theta_c)=0\) under smoothness and uniform curvature gives \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\). Bounded derivatives and \(\|H_c^{-1}\|\leq h^{-1}\) imply \(\sup_c\|\theta_c'\|<\infty\). Bounded outcomes, overlap, bounded features, compactness, smoothness, and uniform curvature therefore imply
\[
 E_P\Psi_c=0,qquad \sup_{c,o}\|\Psi_c(o)\|<\infty,qquad
 \|\Psi_c(o)-\Psi_t(o)\|\leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}|c-t|.
 \tag{32}
\]
For any finite collection of coordinates and penalty values, the ordinary multivariate Lindeberg proof applies because the summands are bounded, giving a centered Gaussian limit with covariance \(\Gamma\). For an increment \(Z_i=\Psi_c(O_i)-\Psi_t(O_i)-E_P[\Psi_c(O)-\Psi_t(O)]\), independence and (32) give coordinatewise
\[
 E_P\left|n^{-1/2}\sum_iZ_i\right|^4
 \leq n^{-1}E_P|Z_1|^4+3(E_P|Z_1|^2)^2
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}|c-t|^4.
 \tag{33}
\]
A dyadic partition and Markov's inequality applied to (33) make the probability of an oscillation larger than \(\varepsilon\) on mesh \(2^{-m}\) summable in \(m\); hence the process is tight in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\). Finite-dimensional convergence identifies its only possible limit as the declared \(G\). Equations (27), (30), and (31) then prove the asserted full-stack weak convergence.

Finally, \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-efficiency}\) identifies \(\psi_c^\theta\) as the canonical gradient at each fixed positive penalty on the common regular softmax submodel. For deterministic \(c_1,\ldots,c_r\), pathwise differentiation is linear, so the canonical gradient of \((\theta_{c_1},\ldots,\theta_{c_r})\) is the stacked vector \((\psi_{c_1}^\theta,\ldots,\psi_{c_r}^\theta)\); its covariance is therefore the joint semiparametric bound. Expansion (27) attains that covariance. The parameter correspondence in \(\textnormal{def:frx-penalty-map}\) is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), while \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-dr-attainment}\) supplies the cited fixed-penalty attainment comparison. Thus the efficiency sentence is a uniform-process extension, not an identification by definition.

By \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\), \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). The definition of \(\upsilon_n\) therefore gives directly
\[
 \sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{34}
\]
Thus
\[
 P(\mathcal E_n)
 =P\left\{\sup_c\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|_{\mathrm{op}}<h/2\right\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), Weyl's inequality and \(\textnormal{ass:uniform-curvature}\) give, simultaneously for all \(c\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c)
 \geq\lambda_{\min}(H_c)-\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|_{\mathrm{op}}>h/2.
\]
Consequently the positive-part ridge in \(\textnormal{def:totalized-hessian}\) is zero, so \(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}=\widehat H_c\) and their inverses agree for every \(c\). Off \(\mathcal E_n\), the definition still gives \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})\geq h/2\), hence a measurable inverse with norm at most \(2/h\). All covariance, multiplier, and regret objects are therefore defined for every sample, while (34) shows that totalization changes none of their limiting laws.

Define the centered oracle multiplier process
\[
 G_n^{\circ}(c)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\{\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)\}.
\]
Conditionally on the data it is Gaussian. The compact-argmax argument in \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\) gives continuity of \(c\mapsto\theta_c\); uniform interiority, smoothness, and curvature then permit differentiation of \(\nabla M_c(\theta_c)=0\), giving \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\). Direct differentiation of the finite-action softmax, together with bounded outcomes, overlap, bounded features, compactness, and the inverse-curvature bound, therefore gives
\[
 E_P\Psi_c=0,\qquad \sup_{c,o}\|\Psi_c(o)\|<\infty,
 \qquad \|\Psi_c(o)-\Psi_t(o)\|\leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}|c-t|.
\]
Applying this direct bound also to products of coordinates, a finite-grid uniform law of large numbers gives
\[
 \sup_{c,t}\left\|n^{-1}\sum_i
 [\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)][\Psi_t(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(t)]^\top
 -\Gamma(c,t)\right\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{35}
\]
Thus every conditional finite-dimensional covariance of \(G_n^{\circ}\) converges to that of \(G\). Moreover, conditionally on the data, its increment variance is at most \(C_{\mathrm{sm}}|c-t|^2\); the fourth moment of a centered Gaussian variable is three times the square of its variance. The same dyadic argument used after (33) proves conditional asymptotic tightness in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\). Hence
\[
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_\xi(G_n^{\circ}\mid O_1^n),\mathcal L(G)\}
 \longrightarrow_{\mathbb P}0.
 \tag{36}
\]

By definition,
\[
 G_n^*(c)-G_n^{\circ}(c)=n^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i\Delta_i(c).
\]
The final conclusion of \(\textnormal{thm:foldwise-replacement}\) says that the conditional expected supremum norm of this difference is \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). For every functional bounded by one and Lipschitz for the supremum norm, its conditional expectation changes by at most that quantity. The triangle inequality in bounded-Lipschitz distance and (36) therefore prove the asserted conditional weak convergence of \(G_n^*\).

For covariance, set \(U_i(c)=\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)\), so \(\widetilde\Psi_i(c)=U_i(c)+\Delta_i(c)\). Cauchy--Schwarz gives uniformly in \(c,t\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left\|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-n^{-1}\sum_iU_i(c)U_i(t)^\top\right\|\\
 &\quad\leq \delta_n\sup_u\{n^{-1}\sum_i\|U_i(u)\|^2\}^{1/2}
       +\delta_n\sup_u\{n^{-1}\sum_i\|U_i(u)\|^2\}^{1/2}+\delta_n^2
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{37}
\]
because \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and the preceding direct bound controls the oracle term. Combining (35) and (37) proves \(\sup_{c,t}\|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-\Gamma(c,t)\|\to_{\mathbb P}0\). Finally, \(\textnormal{lem:ridge-fallback-inactive}\) proves \(P(\mathcal E_n)\to1\) and equality of totalized and ordinary inversion on that event. This also verifies that the same totalized stack is used in covariance and multiplier calculations.

Let \(Z_n(c)\) be the welfare and divergence coordinates of \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau(c)-\tau(c)\}\), and set
\[
 T_n=\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\max_{j\in\{W,K\}}\frac{|Z_{n,j}(c)|}{s_j(c)},
 \qquad
 S=\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\max_{1\leq j\leq d+4}\frac{|G_j(c)|}{s_j(c)}.
\]
Scale regularity makes division by \(s\) continuous and finite on the compact interval. By \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-linearization}\),
\[
 T_n\Rightarrow T:=\sup_c\max_{j\in\{W,K\}}|G_j(c)|/s_j(c),
\]
and \(T\leq S\) almost surely. By \(\textnormal{thm:conditional-multiplier}\), the conditional law of the full bootstrap supremum converges to that of \(S\). Let
\[
 q=\inf\{x:P(S\leq x)\geq1-\alpha\}.
\]
The continuous Gaussian path and scale regularity make \(S<\infty\) almost surely. Choose a continuity point \(r\in(q-\eta/2,q)\) of the distribution function of \(S\). Since \(P(S\leq r)<1-\alpha\), conditional weak convergence implies
\[
 P\{\widehat q_{1-\alpha}\geq r\}\longrightarrow1.
 \tag{38}
\]
On this event, \(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta>q+\eta/2\). Because
\[
 P(T<q+\eta/2)\geq P(S\leq q)\geq1-\alpha,
\]
the portmanteau inequality for the open interval \(( -\infty,q+\eta/2)\), (38), and \(T_n\Rightarrow T\) yield
\[
 \liminf_nP\{T_n\leq\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta\}\geq1-\alpha.
 \tag{39}
\]
No anti-concentration or continuity of the law at its quantile is required; the fixed positive slack supplies the strict separation.

By \(\textnormal{def:frontier-tube}\), the event in (39) is exactly sufficient for both tube inequalities at every \(c\), and therefore implies
\[
 (c,W(\theta_c),K(\theta_c))\in\widehat{\mathcal T}_n
 \quad\text{for all }c\in\mathcal C.
\]
This proves simultaneous coverage. On the same event the inclusion holds at \(c=\widehat c\) for every measurable selector with values in \(\mathcal C\). Hence the simultaneous event is contained in the selected-coordinate coverage event, proving its stated unconditional lower coverage. No conditional-after-selection assertion is made.

Work on the simultaneous tube event from \(\textnormal{thm:postselection-tube}\). Fix \(k\in\mathbb R\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(k)\). By definition, \(K(\theta_c)=k\), so the divergence-coordinate tube inequality gives
\[
 |\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-k|
 =|\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-K(\theta_c)|
 \leq s_K(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n.
\]
Thus \(c\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\), proving \(\mathcal C(k)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal C}_n(k)\). The welfare-coordinate inequality gives
\[
 W(\theta_c)\in
 [\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n,
  \widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)+s_W(c)(\widehat q_{1-\alpha}+\eta)/\sqrt n].
\]
The just-proved membership makes this interval one of those in the union defining \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)\); hence \(W(\theta_c)\in\widehat{\mathcal V}_n(k)\). The argument is algebra on one event already uniform in \(c\), so it holds for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) simultaneously. It uses no derivative, division by a derivative, injectivity, or branch choice. Empty true inverse sections are harmless. This proves the stated specialization of the inverse-set logic directly.

Put \(u_n(c)=\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)\). Interiority gives \(\nabla M_c(\theta_c)=0\). The uniformly continuous third derivative in \(\textnormal{ass:smooth-criterion}\), localization, and Taylor's formula give uniformly in \(c\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_n(c)
 &=M_c(\theta_c)-M_c(\widehat\theta_c)\\
 &=\tfrac12(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)^\top H_c(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)
   +o_{\mathbb P}(\|\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\|^2).
\end{aligned}
\tag{40}
\]
The optimizer expansion in \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-linearization}\) says
\[
 \sup_c\left\|u_n(c)-n^{-1/2}\sum_i\psi_c^\theta(O_i)\right\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad \sup_c\|u_n(c)\|=O_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{41}
\]
Multiplying (40) by \(n\), using boundedness of \(H_c\), and substituting (41) proves the displayed uniform quadratic reduction.

The continuous map \(z\mapsto[c\mapsto\tfrac12z(c)^\top H_cz(c)]\) from \(C(\mathcal C)^d\) to \(C(\mathcal C)\), together with the process limit in \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-linearization}\), yields \(nR_n\Rightarrow Q\). The conditional multiplier theorem gives \(G_{n,\theta}^*\Rightarrow G_\theta\) conditionally in probability. The ridge lemma and Hessian consistency give
\[
 \sup_c\|\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}-H_c\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
The same continuous-map argument, now conditional on the data, proves \(Q_n^*\Rightarrow Q\).

To make the band assertion explicit, let \(r:\mathcal C\to(0,\infty)\) be any prespecified continuous function bounded away from zero, and define the continuous supremum functional \(\mathcal S_r(f)=\sup_cf(c)/r(c)\). If \(q^*_{r,1-\alpha}\) is the conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\mathcal S_r(Q_n^*)\), the same continuity-point argument as in (38)--(39) gives
\[
 \liminf_nP\left\{R_n(c)\leq \frac{r(c)}n\{q^*_{r,1-\alpha}+\eta\}
                  \text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C\right\}\geq1-\alpha.
 \tag{42}
\]
Thus (42) also holds at every measurable \(\widehat c\in\mathcal C\). This is the claimed simultaneous upper-band calibration; the fixed slack handles possible atoms of the quadratic supremum law.

Finally, under \(\textnormal{def:frx-penalty-map}\), \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The fixed-coordinate quadratic form agrees with the cited conclusions in \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-regret}\) and \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-dr-attainment}\). The new statement is the uniform process and shared-multiplier calibration, not a redefinition of the fixed-penalty result.

Fix a deterministic \(c\in\mathcal C\). Evaluation at \(c\) is a continuous linear map on \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\). Applying it to \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-linearization}\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c)\Rightarrow G_\theta(c).
\]
Evaluation at \(c\) applied to \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-regret}\) gives
\[
 nR_n(c)\Rightarrow\tfrac12G_\theta(c)^\top H_cG_\theta(c).
\]
Under \(\textnormal{def:frx-penalty-map}\), restriction to the common softmax class identifies \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The efficient fixed-penalty optimizer and quadratic-regret conclusions are exactly the published results recorded in \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-dr-attainment}\) and \(\textnormal{lem:frx-fixed-regret}\). Thus the proposition is a specialization and sign-normalization check, not an additional asymptotic claim.

theorem.statement:
There are events whose probabilities tend to one on which, simultaneously for \(1\leq\ell\leq L\) and \(u\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\left\|E_P\left[\partial_\theta^u\{\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}(O)-v_\theta(O)\}\mid\text{the training complement of }\mathcal I_\ell\right]\right\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}r_{m,n}r_{e,n}
\]
and
\[
 \left\|F_{\ell,u}\right\|_{P,2}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}).
\]
The empirical criteria and their first two parameter derivatives converge uniformly to their population counterparts, the global optimizer localizes uniformly, and \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). With the totalized-Hessian convention,
\[
 \delta_n\leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
Moreover \(\Lambda_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and, conditionally on the complete data,
\[
 E_\xi\left[\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\left\|n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\left[\widetilde\Psi_i(c)-\{\Psi_c(O_i)-\overline\Psi_n(c)\}\right]\right\|\,\middle|\,O_1,\ldots,O_n\right]=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
These conclusions require no independence among the overlapping training complements.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix a fold \(\ell\), condition on the observations outside \(\mathcal I_\ell\), and abbreviate
\[
 \delta m_a=\widehat m_a^{(-\ell)}-m_a,
 \qquad
 \delta e_a=\widehat e_a^{(-\ell)}-e_a.
\]
The clipping in \(\textnormal{def:crossfit-estimator}\), \(\textnormal{ass:bounded-outcome}\), and \(\textnormal{ass:overlap}\) give
\[
 |m_a|\leq B,\quad |\widehat m_a^{(-\ell)}|\leq B,
 \quad e_a\geq\epsilon,quad
 \widehat e_a^{(-\ell)}\geq\epsilon/2.
 \tag{1}
\]
Finite \(\mathcal A\), \(\textnormal{ass:bounded-features}\), and compactness of \(\Theta\) imply, by differentiating the softmax quotient, that for \(u=0,1,2,3\),
\[
 \sup_{a,x,\theta}\|\partial_\theta^u\pi_\theta(a\mid x)\|\leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, each derivative is a finite sum of products of centered features \(q_a-\sum_r\pi_\theta(r\mid x)q_r\), and every such factor is bounded by twice the feature bound. The benchmark assumptions ensure that the displayed softmax and all logarithms used below are well defined.

Conditional on the training complement, the evaluation observation has law \(P\) by \(\textnormal{ass:iid}\). Direct conditional expectation, using \(E_P[Y-m_A(X)\mid A,X]=0\), gives, for every \(u\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &E_P\left[\partial_\theta^u\{\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta\}\mid X,\text{training}\right]\\
 &\quad=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\partial_\theta^u\pi_\theta(a\mid X)\,delta m_a(X)
       \left\{1-\frac{e_a(X)}{\widehat e_a^{(-\ell)}(X)}\right\}\\
 &\quad=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\partial_\theta^u\pi_\theta(a\mid X)
       \frac{\delta m_a(X)\delta e_a(X)}{\widehat e_a^{(-\ell)}(X)}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
Thus (1), (2), Cauchy--Schwarz, and the two nuisance-rate assumptions imply
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\left\|E_P\left[\partial_\theta^u
 (\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta)\mid\text{training}\right]\right\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}\sum_a\|\delta m_a\|_{P_X,2}\|\delta e_a\|_{P_X,2}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}r_{m,n}r_{e,n}
 \tag{4}
\]
on events whose probabilities tend to one. This is the claimed orthogonal product bias.

For the stochastic radius, elementary algebra gives
\[
 \widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta
 =\sum_a\pi_\theta(a\mid X)\delta m_a(X)
 +\pi_\theta(A\mid X)\left[(Y-m_A(X))left\{\frac1{\widehat e_A^{(-\ell)}(X)}-\frac1{e_A(X)}\right\}
 -\frac{\delta m_A(X)}{\widehat e_A^{(-\ell)}(X)}\right].
 \tag{5}
\]
Only the softmax weights depend on \(\theta\). Since
\[
 \left|\frac1{\widehat e_a^{(-\ell)}}-\frac1{e_a}\right|
 \leq \frac{2}{\epsilon^2}|\delta e_a|,
 \tag{6}
\]
(1), (2), (5), and the finiteness of \(\mathcal A\) yield the pointwise envelope inequality
\[
 F_{\ell,u}(O)
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}\left\{\sum_a|\delta m_a(X)|
       +\sum_a|\delta e_a(X)|
       +|\delta m_A(X)|\right\}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently the exact envelope conclusion of \(\textnormal{lem:softmax-path-entropy}\), not merely a supremum of separate \(L^2(P)\) norms, gives
\[
 \|F_{\ell,u}\|_{P,2}\leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}).
 \tag{8}
\]
This distinction is essential because, conditional on the training complement,
\[
 E_P\left[|\mathcal I_\ell|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_\ell}F_{\ell,u}(O_i)^2\,\middle|\,\text{training}\right]
 =\|F_{\ell,u}\|_{P,2}^2.
 \tag{9}
\]
Conditional Markov's inequality applied to (9), followed by a union bound over the fixed number \(L\) of folds, therefore proves
\[
 \max_{\ell,u}|\mathcal I_\ell|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_\ell}F_{\ell,u}(O_i)^2
 =O_{\mathbb P}\{(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n})^2\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
No independence between training complements is invoked. Fold balance converts (10) into the corresponding full-sample bound.

We next establish localization and the components of \(\upsilon_n\). The polynomial covering bound in \(\textnormal{lem:softmax-path-entropy}\), conditional symmetrization within each evaluation fold, and its envelope bound (8) imply
\[
 \max_{\ell,u}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
 \left|\mathbb G_{n,\ell}\left(\partial_\theta^u(\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta)
 -E_P[\partial_\theta^u(\widehat v_\theta^{(-\ell)}-v_\theta)\mid\text{training}]\right)\right|
 =O_{\mathbb P}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n})=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \tag{11}
\]
where \(\mathbb G_{n,\ell}=|\mathcal I_\ell|^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_\ell}(\delta_{O_i}-P)\). To see the last display directly, take an \(L^2(P)\) net at dyadic radii, apply the conditional Rademacher second-moment bound at each finite net, and sum the resulting geometric increments; the entropy bound makes the sum at most a constant times the envelope norm in (8). Markov's inequality then gives (11).

The oracle score classes \(\{\partial_\theta^u v_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) and the corresponding divergence-integrand classes are uniformly bounded and Lipschitz in \(\theta\) by (1), (2), benchmark positivity, and compactness. A finite-grid argument therefore gives their uniform laws of large numbers. Combining those laws with (4), (10), and (11) yields, for \(u=0,1,2\),
\[
 \sup_{c\in\mathcal C,\theta\in\Theta}
 \|\partial_\theta^u\widehat M_c(\theta)-\partial_\theta^uM_c(\theta)\|
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{12}
\]

Global uniqueness is now used explicitly. First, the map \(c\mapsto\theta_c\) is continuous. Indeed, if \(c_j\to c\), compactness of \(\Theta\) gives a convergent subsequence \(\theta_{c_{j_k}}\to\theta_*\). Passing to the limit in \(M_{c_{j_k}}(\theta_{c_{j_k}})\geq M_{c_{j_k}}(\vartheta)\) for every \(\vartheta\in\Theta\) shows that \(\theta_*\) maximizes \(M_c\), and \(\textnormal{ass:unique-optimizer}\) gives \(\theta_*=\theta_c\). Every subsequential limit is the same, proving continuity. For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), continuity of \(M_c(\theta)\), compactness of \(\mathcal C\times\Theta\), and uniqueness then give the strictly positive uniform separation
\[
 \kappa_\varepsilon
 =\inf_{\substack{c\in\mathcal C,\theta\in\Theta\\
                   \|\theta-\theta_c\|\geq\varepsilon}}
   \{M_c(\theta_c)-M_c(\theta)\}>0.
 \tag{13}
\]
If the infimum were zero, a convergent minimizing subsequence would contradict uniqueness at its limiting \(c\). The zeroth-order case of (12) and global optimality of \(\widehat\theta_c\) now imply
\[
 \sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{14}
\]
Uniform interiority makes all estimated optimizers interior with probability tending to one. The second-order case of (12), (14), and uniform continuity of the population Hessian give
\[
 \sup_c\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{15}
\]
The first-order cases applied separately to welfare and divergence similarly give
\[
 \sup_c\|\nabla\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-a_c\|
 +\sup_c\|\nabla\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c)-g_c\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(16) prove \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).

It remains to pass from criteria to the complete influence stack. The curvature assumption and Weyl's eigenvalue inequality imply for the ridge in \(\textnormal{def:totalized-hessian}\)
\[
 0\leq\{h/2-\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H_c)\}_+
 \leq\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|,
 \quad
 \|\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}}-H_c\|
 \leq2\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|.
 \tag{17}
\]
Moreover \(\|(\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\|\leq2/h\), \(\|H_c^{-1}\|\leq1/h\), and the resolvent identity gives
\[
 \| (\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}-H_c^{-1}\|
 \leq4h^{-2}\|\widehat H_c-H_c\|.
 \tag{18}
\]
Apply (7), (10), and the smooth finite-dimensional product rule to every component in \(\textnormal{def:joint-influence}\). Path evaluation at \(\widehat\theta_c\) costs at most \(C_{\mathrm{sm}}\sup_c\|\widehat\theta_c-\theta_c\|\), empirical gradients cost the corresponding terms of \(\upsilon_n\), and inverse-Hessian replacement is bounded by (18). Thus, if \(\widehat\Psi_i^{\mathrm{raw}}(c)\) denotes the plug-in stack before empirical centering,
\[
 \sup_c\left\{n^{-1}\sum_i
 \|\widehat\Psi_i^{\mathrm{raw}}(c)-\Psi_c(O_i)\|^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
 \tag{19}
\]
The product term in (19) comes from (4); it is retained separately although the product is asymptotically no larger than the displayed sum. Empirical centering is an \(L^2(\mathbb P_n)\) contraction: for any vector array \(z_i\),
\[
 n^{-1}\sum_i\|z_i-\overline z\|^2
 =n^{-1}\sum_i\|z_i\|^2-\|\overline z\|^2
 \leq n^{-1}\sum_i\|z_i\|^2.
 \tag{20}
\]
With \(z_i(c)=\widehat\Psi_i^{\mathrm{raw}}(c)-\Psi_c(O_i)\), (20) turns (19) into the asserted bound for \(\delta_n\), which tends to zero by the nuisance assumptions and (14)--(16).

For completeness, we prove the path modulus under precisely the assumptions missing from the earlier dependency list. On the event furnished by (13)--(15), the empirical global optimizer is unique, lies in the uniform interior neighborhood, and its Hessian has minimum eigenvalue at least \(h/2\). Differentiating its score equation gives
\[
 \widehat H_c\widehat\theta_c'=-\nabla\widehat K(\widehat\theta_c),
 \tag{21}
\]
so (1), (2), and (15) imply \(\sup_c\|\widehat\theta_c'\|=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\). The same product-rule bounds, (17)--(18), and the bounded third derivatives then show
\[
 \left\{n^{-1}\sum_i\|\Delta_i(c)-\Delta_i(t)\|^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \leq O_{\mathbb P}(1)|c-t|,
 \tag{22}
\]
uniformly in \(c,t\), hence \(\Lambda_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\). This derivation uses global uniqueness, uniform interiority, and the totalization rule explicitly.

Condition on the complete data. The multiplier difference is a centered Gaussian process with canonical semimetric at most \(\widehat d_n\). Cover the interval by a dyadic chain of \(\widehat d_n\)-nets. The elementary bound \(E\max_{1\leq j\leq N}|Z_j|\leq\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2N)}\) for centered Gaussian variables with variances at most \(\sigma^2\), obtained from \(E e^{tZ_j}\leq e^{t^2\sigma^2/2}\) and optimization over \(t\), gives after summing the chain
\[
 E_\xi\sup_c\left\|n^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i\Delta_i(c)\right\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}\delta_n
 \sqrt{1+\log\{1+\Lambda_n\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C)/\delta_n\}},
 \tag{23}
\]
with value zero at \(\delta_n=0\). Because \(x\sqrt{1+\log(1+A/x)}\to0\) as \(x\downarrow0\) for every bounded \(A\), (22), \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and (23) prove the asserted conditional expectation bound. The proof conditioned on one evaluation fold only for (3)--(11), combined folds by a finite union bound, and conditioned on all data only after the influence array was formed. It nowhere treats overlapping training complements as independent.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}\|\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau(c)-\tau(c)\}-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n(\psi^\theta_c(O_i),\psi^W_c(O_i),\psi^K_c(O_i))\|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Jointly, the two implemented-rule evaluation errors satisfy \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}|\sqrt n\{\widehat W(\widehat\theta_c)-W(\widehat\theta_c)\}-n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\phi^W_c(O_i)|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and the analogous statement with \(K\) and \(\phi^K_c\). Therefore the full stack converges in \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\) to \(G\) with kernel \(\Gamma\), and at every finite deterministic collection of penalty coordinates the optimizer coordinates jointly attain the semiparametric covariance bound generated by \(\psi_c^\theta\). On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel, set FangRidderXie2026's optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). This is the uniform-in-penalty extension of the fixed-penalty efficient influence bound in its Theorem 1 and the efficient doubly robust optimizer limit in its Theorem 5.

proposed.statement: Construct \(\widetilde\Psi_i\), \(\widehat\Gamma\), and \(G_n^*\) with the common total ridge convention \((\widehat H_c^{\mathrm{tot}})^{-1}\). Under the explicit uniform estimated-influence replacement condition \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), the covariance estimator is uniformly consistent, \(\sup_{c,t\in\mathcal C}\|\widehat\Gamma(c,t)-\Gamma(c,t)\|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), and the conditional law of the stacked shared-multiplier process \(G_n^*\) given \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) converges in probability in bounded-Lipschitz distance on \(C(\mathcal C)^{d+4}\) to the law of \(G\). The event \(\mathcal E_n\) has probability tending to one and, on that event, the total ridge convention equals ordinary Hessian inversion simultaneously for every \(c\in\mathcal C\).

proposed.statement: The entire penalized-regret path has the uniform second-order reduction \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}|nR_n(c)-\tfrac12\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi^\theta_c(O_i)\}^\top H_c\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi^\theta_c(O_i)\}|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so \(nR_n\Rightarrow Q\) in \(C(\mathcal C)\). Conditionally on the data, the totalized process \(Q_n^*\Rightarrow Q\), and conditional quantiles of continuous supremum functionals of \(Q_n^*\), enlarged by the fixed slack \(\eta\), yield simultaneous upper bands for \(R_n(c)\) that remain valid at \(\widehat c\). On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel, set FangRidderXie2026's optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). This process is the uniform-in-penalty extension of its Theorem 2 fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law and its Theorem 5 efficient doubly robust quadratic-regret limit.

prose_updates.tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel of FangRidderXie2026, the direct KL penalty satisfies \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and the reported normalized preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The note proves the formerly open foldwise replacement theorem: conditional bias is \(O_{\mathbb P}(r_{m,n}r_{e,n})\), the empirical nuisance envelope is \(O_{\mathbb P}(r_{m,n}+r_{e,n})\), global uniqueness yields uniform argmax localization, and totalized smooth plug-in composition gives \(\delta_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and conditional multiplier replacement without treating overlapping folds as independent. These inputs deliver the joint uniform optimizer--welfare--divergence influence process, uniformly consistent covariance kernel, shared conditional multiplier bootstrap, a post-selection-valid frontier tube, set-valued inversion, and uniform Hessian-quadratic regret calibration. The measurable ridge fallback is defined on every sample and is uniformly inactive with probability tending to one.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorems 1, 2, and 5 give fixed-positive-penalty efficiency, optimizer limits, and quadratic regret. Generic indexed inference supplies reusable process tools but does not verify fold-specific learned influences composed with the same-sample implicit optimizer path. The missing step was the quantitative empirical replacement bound and path tightness under overlapping training complements.
project_justification.niche: The common softmax submodel permits an explicit orthogonal product-bias calculation, a shrinking \(L^2(P)\) envelope for derivatives through order two, a compact-argmax separation argument based on global uniqueness, and a totalized inverse-Hessian composition bound. Together these verify a single stacked multiplier law that preserves dependence across every displayed preference and coordinate.
project_justification.fill: The proved replacement theorem establishes \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), \(\delta_n\leq C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and \(\Lambda_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Conditional Gaussian chaining then makes the multiplier replacement negligible. Uniform score expansion, covariance consistency, simultaneous tube coverage after every measurable preference choice, eventwise set inversion, and the \(n\)-scaled Hessian-quadratic regret process follow under the declared path-uniform assumptions.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of balanced folds is used. Conditional on each training complement, clipped outcome and propensity learners have uniform \(L^2(P_X)\) errors of orders \(r_{m,n}\) and \(r_{e,n}\); orthogonality makes the conditional score bias order \(r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\), and \(\sqrt n r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\to0\). Fold conclusions are combined by a fixed-fold union bound, not by asserting independence of overlapping training complements.

prose_updates.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the admissible-rule framework and three-arm commitment-savings frontier. Its Theorem 1 gives the fixed-penalty efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, and Theorem 5 efficient doubly robust optimizer and regret limits. On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass, the mapping is \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The advance here is uniform inference over the direct penalty path under explicitly stronger uniform interiority, smoothness, and curvature. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies a generic estimated-score multiplier architecture; this note verifies its difficult replacement inputs by foldwise doubly robust algebra, the actual \(L^2(P)\) envelope bound, global argmax localization, totalized inverse-Hessian stability, and conditional Gaussian chaining. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies the standard cross-fitting and product-rate architecture. ChenFang2019 motivates second-order calibration under first-order degeneracy. The inverse correspondence is proved eventwise and agrees with the logic of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024; it is a reporting corollary, not part of the novelty kernel.
prose_updates.interpretation: One shared multiplier draw approximates the entire optimizer, oracle-frontier, and implemented-rule evaluation process. A planner may inspect the plotted welfare--divergence curve and then choose any measurable penalty without forfeiting the unconditional simultaneous guarantee. If a divergence level has several compatible penalties, the set-valued inverse retains all branches. The separate quadratic process reports the statistical loss in penalized welfare at the fitted rule on the natural \(n^{-1}\) scale.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The foldwise replacement bottleneck is closed under the declared fixed-dimensional, bounded, uniformly overlapping model. The proof needs global uniqueness for the uniform separation \(\kappa_\varepsilon>0\), compact argmax localization, and \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\); local curvature and interiority alone would not suffice. It uses the \(L^2(P)\) norm of the pointwise envelope \(F_{\ell,u}\) in the conditional Markov step and never substitutes a supremum of pointwise function norms. The totalized Hessian is essential for finite-sample definition and becomes ordinary inversion only on \(\mathcal E_n\). The result excludes vanishing penalties, weak overlap, growing dimension, adaptive sampling, and nonunique optimizers. The tube targets the oracle frontier, while separately stacked coordinates describe implemented-rule evaluation; the quadratic theorem concerns penalized regret rather than unpenalized welfare loss.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The result is a uniform-in-penalty inference theorem on a fixed finite-dimensional benchmark-centered softmax subclass, not a broader identification result or a minimax claim. Its novel technical component is the proved foldwise same-sample-path replacement bound and the resulting conditional shared-multiplier validity. Path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, global uniqueness, and a positive curvature floor remain explicit maintained assumptions stronger than fixed-penalty regularity. Set-valued inversion and deterministic-penalty reduction are application and sanity corollaries. No result is asserted for \(c\to0\), weak overlap, nonunique optima, growing feature dimension, or optimal tube width.
